source.title: Locally Estimated Global Perturbations are Better than Local Perturbations for Federated Sharpness-aware Minimization
source.authors: Zi-Qing Fan; Sheng-Chao Hu; Jiangchao Yao; Gang Niu; Ya Zhang; Masashi Sugiyama; Yan-Feng Wang

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses sharpness-aware minimization as a training method and treats flatter minima as beneficial for generalization. Its experiments compare federated methods, but do not test any listed version of the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test accuracy and global sharpness for its federated methods. These results concern federated sharpness minimization and general performance, not the specific behaviors measured by V1–V8. The paper also cites generalization findings from prior work; those citations are not rows.
record.test_reason: Tables 2 and 3 compare adaptive server optimization, FedAdam, with nonadaptive FedAvg on held-out image classification. This bears on V4 in a federated setting, although all clients use SGD and optimizer tuning is limited. The SAM experiments do not test V7: they measure unscaled loss sharpness, without train-test gaps or comparisons of generalization measures.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors identify discrepancies between local and global sharpness minimization under heterogeneous federated data, propose estimating global perturbations from successive received global models, prove convergence results, and report improved benchmark performance and computational efficiency for FedLESAM and its variants.
record.recipe_differences: Federated SAM-based method using prior and current global model differences to estimate perturbations; not the original claim's natural-label generalization experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports outcomes across dataset splits and client participation settings, and states that the perturbation magnitude ρ affects accuracy and convergence.

fits_no_version.finding: FedLESAM and FedSAM reach 81.04±0.19 and 80.10±0.12 accuracy in the recorded CIFAR10 condition.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Locally estimated global perturbations improve accuracy over local SAM perturbations in this federated setting.

fits_no_version.finding: FedLESAM produces smaller global sharpness in Figure 2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Estimating global perturbations can reduce absolute-radius global loss sharpness more effectively than the compared federated SAM methods.

fits_no_version.finding: FedLESAM-S improves average accuracy over Scaffold on all four datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding the proposed global perturbation estimation to Scaffold improves these federated benchmark averages.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 235, 2024
record.problems: The reported main outcomes are test accuracy rather than train-test gaps. Global-sharpness comparisons are described in text and figures without numerical values in the supplied text. The experiments are federated and do not test random-label memorization, width sweeps, or magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 2 and 3 report many additional method-by-dataset-by-split test accuracies; they were not extracted because they do not measure any listed claim version. Figures 3 and 6 show loss-surface visualizations without numerical values in the supplied text.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, chance-level random-label test accuracy, and coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.

Centralized Adam versus SGD; comparable training performance; systematic learning-rate and schedule tuning; broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, optimizer switching, and language modeling. Here adaptation occurs at the federated server while clients use SGD.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover large-batch performance.
Dropout comparisons, small-data effects, underfitting, and interactions with augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus train-test gaps at similarly low training loss, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Identifying and removing memorized examples, retraining, and comparison with random removal.

missing.what: FedAdam-versus-FedAvg test-accuracy pairs for all 16 CIFAR conditions, including uncertainty and client configuration. These establish V4's mixed results. Although rows_left_out declares additional table accuracies omitted, the adaptive-optimizer comparisons need extraction for this verdict.

FedAdam-versus-FedAvg target-domain accuracy pairs for all OfficeHome and DomainNet conditions. Record pretrained ViT-B/32, local SGD, adaptive versus nonadaptive server updates, and the different server learning rates.

record.verdict_notes: V4 evidence concerns adaptive server optimization in federated learning, so its scope should be explicit. The paper gives server learning rates of 0.1 for FedAdam and 1 for other methods, without documenting a systematic optimizer tuning comparison. No original-source exclusion applies.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error as network width increases past the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization under tuning.
Large-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes.
Dropout effects and its interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbation tolerance as a correlate of the train-test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: FedLESAM
rows.operation_detail: Trained with locally estimated global perturbations; test accuracy reported after 800 rounds.
rows.note: Test accuracy is reported, but no train-test gap is given.
rows.check: The accuracy and condition match Table 2. This is the proposed method's benchmark performance and should not be a claim-evidence row. FedLESAM is a training algorithm, not a model architecture.

rows.subject: FedSAM
rows.operation_detail: Trained with local sharpness-aware perturbations; test accuracy reported after 800 rounds.
rows.note: Comparator result; test accuracy does not measure a train-test gap.
rows.check: The accuracy and condition match Table 2, but this SAM-method comparator does not measure any listed version.

rows.subject: FedAvg
rows.operation_detail: Trained without a SAM perturbation; test accuracy reported after 800 rounds.
rows.note: Reference method; test accuracy does not measure a train-test gap.
rows.check: Retain as the nonadaptive comparator for the missing FedAdam result: FedAvg reaches 79.52±0.13 versus FedAdam's 77.08±0.31. The relevant comparison concerns server optimization; both use local SGD. A train-test gap is unnecessary for V4's held-out-performance comparison.

source_check.correct: Retain the control value 79.52±0.13; state=cannot_determine for this standalone control. The paired FedAdam result is 77.08±0.31, supporting V4 for this condition.
source_check.locator_found: Table 2, upper block, CIFAR10, Dirichlet β=0.6; experimental setup in Section 6.1 and Appendix E.1.
source_check.problem: The control accuracy alone does not establish an adaptive-optimizer disadvantage.

rows.subject: FedLESAM
rows.operation_detail: Measured global sharpness during training; authors describe it as much smaller than the compared federated SAM methods.
rows.baseline: FedAvg, FedSAM, FedGAMMA, MoFedSAM, FedSMOO; numerical values not stated in text
rows.note: The text describes a relative sharpness result, not a magnitude-aware sharpness measure or train-test gap.
rows.check: Correctly unlinked. Section 2.2 defines sharpness using an absolute L2 perturbation radius and loss increase, rather than magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance and training error. Figure 2 does not relate this measure to train-test gaps.

rows.subject: FedLESAM-S
rows.size_stated: ResNet-18 backbone for CIFAR10/100; ViT-B/32 backbone for OfficeHome and DomainNet
rows.operation_detail: Compared averaged test accuracy with its base method and other variants across four datasets.
rows.baseline: FedAvg, Scaffold, and FedDyn base methods: 75.96, 41.69, 77.99, 70.25 respectively
rows.note: The table reports aggregate test accuracy by dataset, not train-test gaps.
rows.check: The FedLESAM-S values are correct, but its corresponding Scaffold baselines are 78.80, 44.21, 78.93, and 71.62. The recorded baselines are FedAvg values. This bundles four datasets and reports method performance outside the listed versions.
